ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the lines $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at point $O$, $\angle COE$ is a right angle, $OF$ bisects $\angle AOE$, $\angle COF = 28^\circ$. Find the measure of $\angle BOE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle COE$ is a right angle and $\angle COF=28^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle EOF=90^\circ-28^\circ=62^\circ$,\\
since $OF$ bisects $\angle AOE$,\\
it follows that $\angle AOF=\angle EOF=62^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle EOB=180^\circ-62^\circ-62^\circ=\boxed{56^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached diagram, AB is a straight horizontal line through O, with A on the left and B on the right. Line CD also passes through O, with C above-left of O and D below-right of O. Rays OC, OF, and OE lie above line AB; in the upper half-plane their order from left to right is OC, OF, OE, then OB. The right-angle marker indicates ∠COE is 90°. Reasoning: Given ∠COE = 90° and ∠COF = 28°, the remaining angle between OE and OF is ∠EOF = 90° - 28° = 62°. Since OF bisects ∠AOE, the two parts are equal, so ∠AOF = ∠EOF = 62°. Therefore ∠AOE = 62° + 62° = 124°. Because OA and OB are opposite rays on the straight line AB, ∠AOE and ∠BOE form a linear pair. Hence ∠BOE = 180° - 124° = 56°.
